members.name: opening_range_breakout_30_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 100 constituents on NSE + Bank NIFTY index
members.thesis: The 30-minute Opening Range (09:15-09:45 IST) is a more robust version of the 15-min ORB. The additional 15 minutes of price discovery reduces false breakouts by ~25% compared to 15-min ORB because more institutional orders have been executed, providing a truer reflection of the day's equilibrium zo
filters: India_VIX between 14-25; moderate VIX is ideal for ORB
entry only after 09:45; no new entries after 12:00
breakout bar volume > 2.5x average OR-period bar volume
SGX Nifty direction pre-market should align with breakout direction
bid-ask spread < 0.05%
weaknesses: Later entry (09:45+) means less time for the trade to develop within the session — hold period is compressed
The 2-bar confirmation filter further delays entry, often missing 10-15% of the initial breakout move
On days with large opening gaps (>1.5%), the 30-min OR may be too wide for the measured move target to be realistic
members.prior_art: 30-min ORB is a variant discussed by Mark Fisher (ACD Method, 'The Logical Trader'). Toby Crabel's work covers multiple OR periods (5, 15, 30, 60 min). Indian adaptation is less documented for 30-min

members.name: orb_5min_v1
members.thesis: The 5-minute opening range (high and low of 09:15-09:20) captures the initial price discovery auction. Breakout above/below this range with volume confirmation signals institutional direction for the session. The 5-min ORB is the fastest variant — it works best on high-conviction gap days where inst
entry_long: close > vwap (above VWAP for additional confirmation)
members.exit_stop: close re-enters ORB range (crosses below ORB_high for longs, above ORB_low for shorts) OR midpoint of ORB range
filters: India_VIX between 12 and 22 (need vol for breakout but not chaos)
enter between 09:20-09:45 IST; breakout must occur within 25 mins of range formation
breakout bar volume > 1.5x 20-bar SMA
NIFTY 50 not limit-down or circuit-breaker; gap direction aligned with breakout preferred
bid-ask < 0.05%
weaknesses: The 5-minute range is very narrow (often 0.2-0.4%), making it susceptible to noise-driven false breakouts; win rate is below 50%
On low-gap days (<0.2%), the 5-min range is compressed and nearly any price movement triggers a breakout, most of which fail
The strategy requires very fast execution (within seconds of breakout) to avoid slippage; delayed entry significantly reduces the reward-to-risk ratio
members.prior_art: Crabel (1990) 'Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns'; Fisher (2002) 5-min ORB. Indian market ORB studies by Choudhary & Saini (2015).

members.name: opening_range_breakout_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 100 constituents on NSE + NIFTY 50 index futures
members.thesis: The classic 15-minute Opening Range Breakout (ORB) captures the directional resolution of early-session uncertainty. The first 15 minutes (09:15-09:30 IST) establish a range as institutional pre-market orders, overnight gap adjustments, and global cue reactions settle. A breakout above/below this ra
entry_long: volume on breakout bar > SUM(volume, 15) / 15 * 2.0 (2x avg first-15-min bar volume)
members.exit_target: 1.0 * OR_range from breakout level (measured move equal to OR range)
members.exit_stop: OR_mid (midpoint of opening range) — if price retreats to OR midpoint, breakout failed
filters: India_VIX < 25; ORB works best in moderate vol environments (14-22)
entry only after 09:30 IST; no new entries after 12:00
breakout bar volume > 2x average first-15-min bar volume
prefer breakout direction aligned with global cue (SGX Nifty direction pre-market)
bid-ask spread < 0.06%
weaknesses: False breakouts are the primary failure mode — price breaks OR, triggers entry, then reverses into the range
ORB works best in trending markets; in range-bound, choppy days, both sides of the OR get hit (double loss)
The first breakout after OR is often the most crowded trade — many traders use ORB, reducing edge from crowding
members.prior_art: Opening Range Breakout is one of the oldest day trading strategies (Toby Crabel, 1990 'Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns'). Mark Fisher's ACD method is a variation. Extremely well-documented.

members.name: orb_narrow_range_v1
members.thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is narrower than the previous 4 sessions' opening ranges (NR4 condition on ORB), the subsequent breakout has higher follow-through because narrow opening ranges signal consensus/compression before a directional move. NR4 ORB days have ~12% higher breakout success rat
entry_long: NR4_condition == True (today's ORB is narrowest in 4 sessions)
members.exit_target: 3.0 * ORB_range_15 from breakout level (wider target due to compression-expansion expectation)
members.exit_stop: opposite side of ORB range (ORB_low for longs, ORB_high for shorts) — NR range = tight stop
filters: India_VIX between 12 and 20 (NR days coincide with low-moderate VIX)
enter between 09:30-10:30 IST; NR breakouts that don't trigger in first hour rarely work
breakout bar volume > 1.3x 20-bar SMA
none (NR breakout can go either way; the compression IS the setup)
bid-ask < 0.04%
weaknesses: NR4 condition is infrequent — occurs on ~20% of trading days for any given stock, requiring scanning the full NIFTY 50 universe for signals
Narrow ranges can also indicate low interest/liquidity rather than compression before expansion, leading to low-volume false breakouts
The 3x range target is ambitious; on many NR4 days, the move extends only 1.5-2x the range before stalling, and the wide trailing stop gives back gains
members.prior_art: Crabel (1990) NR4/NR7 patterns; Connors & Raschke (1996) 'Street Smarts' on narrow range breakouts. Adapted from daily to intraday opening range context.

members.name: orb_wide_range_fade_v1
members.thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is wider than 2x the 20-day average ORB range, the initial move has over-extended — the opening auction was dominated by emotional retail order flow, and institutional mean-reversion will pull price back toward the ORB midpoint. Wide opening ranges are the OPPOSITE o
entry_long: RSI_14 < 25 (oversold at bottom of wide range)
entry_short: RSI_14 > 75 (overbought at top of wide range)
members.exit_target: ORB_mid (midpoint of wide range — mean reversion target)
members.exit_stop: close beyond ORB extreme by 0.2 * ORB_range_15 (range extension) OR 0.4% from entry
filters: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX wide ranges may continue expanding
enter 09:30-11:00 IST; wide range fading works best when institutions arrive post-open
opening 15-min volume > 1.5x average (confirming wide range was driven by real flow)
NIFTY not in extreme trend (>2%); on strong trend days, wide ranges continue
bid-ask < 0.05%
weaknesses: Fading wide ranges is contrarian; when the wide range IS the breakout (news-driven, institutional-driven), the fade loses big as price extends the range
Wide range days are infrequent (~10-15% of sessions), making this a low-frequency supplement strategy
The ORB midpoint target may not be reached on days where price consolidates near the extreme instead of reverting, resulting in time-stop exits with small losses
members.prior_art: Crabel (1990) wide range days (WR4/WR7); Connors (1999) on fading extended ranges. Adapted from daily chart concept to 15-min intraday opening range.

members.name: orb_gap_combo_v1
members.thesis: Combining gap analysis with ORB creates a more powerful signal than either alone. When a stock gaps in a direction AND the 15-min ORB breakout is in the same direction as the gap, the probability of sustained follow-through jumps to ~65% (vs ~52% for ORB alone and ~55% for gap continuation alone). T
entry_long: close > ORB_high_15 (ORB breakout up = aligned with gap)
triple_aligned == True (gap + ORB + NIFTY all bullish)
entry_short: close < ORB_low_15 (ORB breakdown = aligned with gap)
triple_aligned == True (gap + ORB + NIFTY all bearish)
members.exit_target: gap_pct + 1.5 * ORB_range_15 from ORB breakout level (gap extension target)
members.exit_stop: ORB_mid OR price fills 50% of the gap (gap fading = thesis invalidated)
filters: India_VIX between 13 and 22
enter 09:30-10:15 IST; gap + ORB combo must trigger early
breakout bar volume > 1.3x 20-bar SMA
TRIPLE ALIGNMENT REQUIRED: stock gap + stock ORB + NIFTY gap all in same direction
bid-ask < 0.05%
weaknesses: Triple alignment (gap + ORB + NIFTY) is very restrictive; it occurs on only ~20-30% of trading days, making this capital-inefficient as standalone
When the triple-aligned setup fails, it tends to fail hard (large reversal), because the high conviction means larger positions and the reversal traps many participants
The gap extension target (gap + 1.5 * ORB range) can be ambitious; on many aligned days the move extends only through the ORB range before consolidating
members.prior_art: Gap-and-go from Katz & McCormick (2000) + ORB from Crabel (1990). Combined approach discussed in Connors & Sen (2004) but not formalized for Indian markets.

members.name: orb_closing_range_v1
members.universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
members.thesis: The 'Closing Range Breakout' (CRB) applies the ORB concept to the last 30 minutes of the trading day (14:30-15:00 IST), trading the breakout from this range in the final 29 minutes (15:00-15:29). The closing range captures institutional end-of-day positioning: mutual funds that need to deploy cash,
entry_long: session_vwap_dev > 0 (stock above session VWAP — bullish overall)
close_vs_session_range > 0.5 (stock in upper half of day's range)
volume_ratio_closing > 1.0 (closing volume at or above average)
entry_short: session_vwap_dev < 0 (stock below session VWAP — bearish overall)
close_vs_session_range < 0.5 (stock in lower half of day's range)
members.exit_target: 1.5 * CRB_range from CRB_high/low OR close the position at 15:28 IST (whichever comes first)
members.exit_stop: CRB_mid OR 0.5 * CRB_range back inside range OR 0.2% from entry
filters: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX closing sessions are chaotic with wide spreads
STRICT: only enter 15:00-15:20 IST; after 15:20 there isn't enough time for the trade to develop
closing 30-min (14:30-15:00) volume > 0.8x average closing volume
session vwap position confirms direction (above VWAP for longs, below for shorts)
bid-ask < 0.05% (spreads can widen in last 10 mins; verify before entry)
weaknesses: The extremely short holding period (5-25 mins) means the trade has very little time to develop; even successful breakouts may only move 10-15 bps before the mandatory exit
Bid-ask spreads can widen significantly in the last 5-10 minutes of the session, increasing effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, which can eat the entire edge
F&O expiry days (weekly and monthly) create abnormal closing dynamics that can generate false CRB signals; the expiry filter helps but weekly expiry is every Thursday
members.prior_art: Harris (1989) on intraday price patterns; similar concept to 'MOC imbalance trading' (Cushing & Madhavan 2000). CRB is the inverse of ORB, applying the same principle to session close.
